main_text.head: CONRADI GESNERI DE DIFFERENTIIS LINGUARUM observationes.
CAPUT I. De Linguis in genere.
main_text.p: INGVARVM confusionis causa atque historia, in sacris libris traLinguarum cognitio magnæ felicitatis humanæ pars.dita, non est quòd hîc à nobis repetatur. Quemadmodum autem magna infelicitatis humanæ pars fuit sermonis confusio: ita nostris temporibus donum verè divinū & præclarę felicitatis loco judicare debemus, totum ferè orbem terrarum tribus illis in Cruce confecratis linguis, quasGen 11, 1, 9.Luc. 24. 38 passim homines studiosi exercent, denuò conjungi: atque harum cognitione non ea modò, quæ ad hominum commercia, quæq; ad sapientiam humanam pertinent, sed pietatem & Deum, innotescere. Quis enim nescit per universam Europam Latinæ ac Græcæ linguarum usum esse: Hebraicæ verò, sive potiùs Arabicę, in Africa Asiaq; totis ferè, Græcæ etiam in parte earundem. Europa sanè tanto cæteris existimanda est felicior,

page.notes: The marginal notes at right read: "Linguarum cognitio magnæ felicitatis humanæ pars." and the references "Gen 11, 1, 9." and "Luc. 24. 38" as printed (the Genesis reference is partly rubbed; the numbers were read as best as possible). The "A" below the text is a signature-like mark at the foot of the text block. The Gesner title line is set in a black-letter-like small-capital face; transcribed in roman capitals. The first letter "I" of the opening paragraph is a decorative woodcut initial, joined to the word as "INGVARVM". The word "tra-dita" is hyphenated at the line end. Printed ink is faint in places; "Europa" and "Græcæ" readings are uncertain and should be checked against the scan. The top-right "1" is the printed page number.
